hints.title: Row and Column Global Order
hints.text: Each row is sorted and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row. How can this 2D grid be viewed as a single continuous 1D sorted sequence?

hints.title: Virtual Coordinate Flattening
hints.text: An element at virtual 1D index k in an m x n matrix corresponds directly to row k // n and column k % n without copying data.

hints.title: Virtual Index Elimination
hints.text: Treat the m x n matrix as a 1D range from 0 to m * n - 1. Maintain low = 0 and high = m * n - 1. For each midpoint, map coordinates to matrix[mid // n][mid % n]. Compare with target, adjusting low or high until matched or exhausted.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Treats the 2D matrix as a virtual 1D array of length M * N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all M * N elements takes O(M * N) time. Even row-by-row searching takes O(M log N), missing the global sorted property.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Virtual 1D index mapping achieves optimal O(log(M * N)) time without allocating any flattened 1D array, maintaining O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Single search over M * N with coordinate division/modulo, handling empty matrix edge cases, and avoiding redundant array copies.

solutions.approach: Virtual Flattening with Quotient and Remainder
